courses.description: Focuses on major crimes, including their classification, elements of proof, intent, conspiracy, responsibility, parties, and defenses. Emphasizes Virginia law. May include general principles of applicable constitutional law and criminal procedure.

courses.title: Information Technology for the Paralegal
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ITE 115 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Provides extensive instruction on the use of technology in the law office, including word processing tools, spreadsheet programs, database management systems, office management programs, case management programs, electronic mail, the cloud, and use of the Internet in the practice of law.

courses.title: Estate Planning and Probate
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces various devices used to plan an estate, including wills, trust, joint ownership and insurance. Considers various plans in light of family situations and estate objectives. Focuses on practices involving administration of an estate including taxes and preparation of forms.

courses.title: Legal Transactions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an in-depth study of general contract law, including formation, breach, enforcement, and remedies. May include an overview of UCC sales, commercial paper, and collections.

courses.title: Legal Aspects of Business Organizations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies fundamental principles of agency law and the formation of business organizations. Includes sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporation, limited liability companies, and other business entities. Reviews preparation of the documents necessary for the organization and operation of businesses.

courses.title: Elder Law
courses.contact_hours: Credits: 3 Lecture Hours: 3 Lab Hours: 0 Contact Hours: 3
courses.description: Explores the legal issues affecting the elderly population, including Social Security, Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Medicare, Medicaid, long-term care insurance, retirement housing and long-term care options, age discrimination, elder abuse and neglect, and estate and planning issues related to incapacity-guardianship, advanced medical directives, power of attorney, and end-of-life decisions.

courses.title: Bankruptcy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a practical understanding of non-bankruptcy alternatives and the laws of bankruptcy including Chapters 7, 11, 12 and 13 of the Bankruptcy Code. Emphasizes will be placed on preparing petitions, schedules, statements, and other forms.

courses.title: Immigration Law
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to immigration law and policy, giving an overview of the United States legal system that regulates the admission, exclusion, removal, and naturalization of immigrants. Includes issues concerning refugees, asylum seekers, illegal immigrants, and undocumented aliens.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Numerical Control I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on numerical control techniques in metal forming and machine processes. Includes theory and practice in lathe and milling machine computer numerical control program writing, setup and operation. Part I of II.

courses.title: Numerical Control II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on numerical control techniques in metal forming and machine processes. Includes theory and practice in lathe and milling machine computer numerical control program writing, setup and operation. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Geometrical Dimensioning and Tolerancing in Machining
courses.contact_hours: Lecture hours 3 per week.
courses.description: Focuses on basic topics in geometrical dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T). Covers internationally recognized GD&T symbols. Explains the importance of a feature control frame. Teaches the Cartesian coordinate system in relation to precision components. Examines theoretical and practical concepts of geometric controls relative to design, tooling, production, and inspection.

courses.title: Introductory CNC Programming
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces programming of computerized numerical control machines with hands-on programming and operation of CNC machines.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Aided Manufacturing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces computer aided manufacturing (CAM) with emphasis on programming of numerical control machinery. Teaches program writing procedures using proper language and logic and a CAM programming system to produce numerical control code for machines. Teaches basic computer usage, 2 1/2D and 3D CAD-CAM integration, and code-to-machine transfer.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces safety procedures, bench work, hand tools, precision measuring instruments, drill presses, cut-off saws, engine lathes, manual surface grinders, and milling machines. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces safety procedures, bench work, hand tools, precision measuring instruments, drill presses, cut-off saws, engine lathes, manual surface grinders, and milling machines. Part II of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in the operation of the drill press, engine lathe, vertical milling machine, horizontal milling machine, and the surface grinder. Introduces practical heat treatment of directly hardenable steels commonly used in machine shops. Part I of II.

courses.title: Machine Shop Practices IV
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers practice in the operation of the drill press, engine lathe, vertical milling machine, horizontal milling machine, and the surface grinder. Introduces practical heat treatment of directly hardenable steels commonly used in machine shops. Part II of II.

courses.title: Machine Blueprint Reading I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces reading and interpreting blueprints and working drawings. Applies visualization of objects, sketching, and machine terminology. Part I of II.

courses.title: Standards, Measurements and Calculations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents typical mathematical and mechanical problems requiring the use of reference standards such as the Machinery's Handbook for solution. Presents use of the Coordinate Measuring Machine for solution.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Introduction to Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers topics in arithmetic through introduction to variables and equations.

courses.title: Learning Support for Quantitative Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 154
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Quantitative Reasoning (MTH 154). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Learning Support for Statistical Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 credits. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 155
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Statistical Reasoning (MTH 155). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Intermediate Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers topics in algebra.

courses.title: Learning Support for Pre-Calculus
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Corequisite: MTH 161
courses.description: Provides support to ensure success for students co-enrolled in Pre-Calculus (MTH 161). Course will review foundational topics through direct instruction, guided practice, and individualized support.

courses.title: Introduction to Medical Laboratory Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic techniques including design of the health care system, ethics, terminology, calculations, venipuncture and routine urinalysis.

courses.title: Phlebotomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic medical terminology, anatomy, physiology, components of health care delivery and clinical laboratory structure. Teaches techniques of specimen collection, specimen handling, and patient interactions.

courses.title: Clinical Phlebotomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on obtaining blood specimens, processing specimens, managing assignments, assisting with and/or performing specified tests, performing clerical duties and maintaining professional communication. Provides supervised learning in college laboratory/and or cooperating agencies.

courses.title: Clinical Hematology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the cellular elements of blood including blood cell formation, and routine hematological procedures.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Immunology and Serology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles of basic immunology, physiology of the immune system, diseases involving the immune system, as well as serologic procedures.

courses.title: Blood Banking
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week..
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of blood grouping and typing, compatibility testing, antibody screening, component preparation, donor selection, and transfusion reactions and investigation.

courses.title: Clinical Hematology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches advanced study of blood to include coagulation, abnormal bloody formation, and changes seen in various diseases.

courses.title: Clinical Microbiology I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Labortory 3-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches handling, isolation, and identification of pathogenic microorganisms. Emphasizes clinical techniques of bacteriology, mycology, parasitology and virology. Part I of II.

courses.title: Clinical Microbiology II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches handling, isolation, and identification of pathogenic microorganisms. Emphasizes clinical techniques of bacteriology, mycology, parasitology and virology. Part II of II.

courses.title: Clinical Chemistry and Instrumentation I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 6-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces methods of performing biochemical analysis of clinical specimens. Teaches instrumentation involved in a clinical chemistry laboratory, quality control, and the ability to recognize technical problems. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Chemistry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents principles of current special chemistry techniques.

courses.title: Clinical Chemistry Techniques
courses.contact_hours: (3-4 Cr.) Lab 9-12 hours. Total 12-16 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes performing of clinical chemistry methodologies and operation of typical instrumentation in a clinical laboratory or simulated laboratory setting.

courses.title: Clinical Hematology Techniques
courses.contact_hours: (3-4 Cr.) Lab 9-12 hours. Total 12-16 hours per week.
courses.description: Stresses performing hematological and coagulation methods and operation of typical instrumentation in a clinical laboratory or simulated laboratory setting.

courses.title: Clinical Blood Banking Techniques
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 12 hours per week. Credits 4 hours.
courses.description: Provides training in techniques, procedures, and interpretations in Blood Banking in a clinical laboratory or simulated laboratory setting.

courses.title: Clinical Microbiology Techniques II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 12 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes performing of techniques, procedures, and identification of microorganisms in a clinical laboratory or simulated laboratory setting.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Introduction to Engineering Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces professional fields of engineering technology. Covers the work of the engineering technologist, professional ethics, division of industrial practice, and engineering problem solving with hand calculator and computer applications.

courses.title: Materials for Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the nature, structure, properties, and typical applications of metallic, polymeric, ceramic, and composite materials. Focuses on applications of materials as well as the behavior of materials subjected to external stresses. Addresses as required the earth's limited material resources, energy efficient materials, dependence on foreign sources of materials, material systems, thermal processing, and electronic-related materials.

courses.title: Computer Programming for Technologists
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces computer software and programming. Covers programming for the microcomputer using high level languages. Teaches computer solutions of mathematical problems in applications such as circuit analysis and static equilibrium.

courses.title: Mechanics I - Statics for Engineering Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches Newton's laws, resultants and equilibrium of force systems, trusses and frames, determination of centroids, and distributed loads and moments of inertia. Introduces dry friction and force systems in space.

courses.title: Mechanics II - Strength of Mat. for Eng. Tech
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the concepts of stress and strain. Provides an analysis of stresses and deformations in loaded members, connectors, shafts, beams, columns, and combined stress.

courses.title: Mechanics Laboratory
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes tension, compression, torsion, bending, fatigue, impact strength, and hardness of materials. Addresses static and dynamic stresses and strains. Provides for statistical evaluation of data. Includes experiments and/or demonstrations.

courses.title: Introduction to Mechatronics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents foundational concepts in mechatronics including analog and digital electronics, sensors, actuators, microprocessors, and microprocessor interfacing to electromechanical systems. Surveys components and measurement equipment used in the design, installation, and repair of mechatronic equipment and circuits. This course is cross-listed with ETR 140 . Credit will not be awarded for both.

courses.title: Industrial Pipefitting
courses.contact_hours: Credits 2 - 3. Lecture 1 - 2 hours. Lab 2 hours. Total 3 - 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the fundamentals of industrial piping installation, components, and layout. Considers the types of pipe and fabrication of piping systems, as well as the methods used to connect them.

courses.title: Mechanical Maintenance I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 1-2 hours. Total 3-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of basic maintenance techniques and processes for industrial mechanics and technicians who are installing and maintaining industrial mechanical and power transmission components.

courses.title: Mechanisms
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the purpose and actions of cams, gear trains, levers, and other mechanical devices used to transmit control. Focuses on motions, linkages, velocities, and acceleration of points within a link mechanism; layout method for designing cams and gear grain. Requires preparation of weekly laboratory reports.

courses.title: Piping and Auxiliary Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies threaded pipe, welded pipe, isometric pipe sketching and layout, gaskets, packing, industrial hoses and tubing, basic steam system operations, automatic and manual valves, and positive displacement pumps.

courses.title: Fluid Power - Hydraulic Systems
courses.contact_hours: Credits 2 - 3. Lecture1 - 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 -4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies hydraulic components and their integration into complex systems including system analysis and troubleshooting. Introduces design considerations necessary for repair and modification. Covers closed loop control and proportional valves with electronic control.

courses.title: Fluid Power - Pneumatic Systems
courses.contact_hours: Credits 2 - 3. Lecture 1 - 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 - 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches pneumatic components, systems and trouble analysis. Introduces basic design for modification and repair. Covers open loop control, fluidics, robotics and computer controls.

courses.title: Principles of Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents principles, methods, and problems involved in marketing to consumers and organizational buyers. Discusses problems and policies connected with distribution and sale of products, pricing, promotion, and buyer motivation. Examines variations of marketing research, legal, social, ethical, e-commerce, and international considerations in marketing.

courses.title: Principles of Selling
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a fundamental, skills-based approach to selling and relationship building. Emphasizes learning effective interpersonal communication skills in all areas of the sales process through skill-building activities. Examines entry-level sales careers in retailing, wholesaling, services and industrial selling.

courses.title: Marketing for Small Business
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the development of the marketing mix for a small business. Includes areas such as product development, pricing, promotion, salesmanship, customer relations, and consumer behavior.

courses.title: Customer Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the concepts of marketing as they relate to customer service. Teaches development of customer service training and implementation of strategies to improve customer relations and service. Includes lecture, role-playing, and case studies.

courses.title: Introduction to Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the discipline of marketing and the need to create customer value and relationships in the marketplace. Presents an overview of the marketing principles and management strategies, along with the analytical tools used by organizations in the creation of a marketing plan.

courses.title: Principles of Advertising
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes the role of advertising in the marketing of goods, services, and ideas. Discusses the different uses of advertising; types of media; how advertising is created; agency functions; and legal, social, and economic aspects of the industry. Introduces advertising display, copy and art work preparation, printing and selection of media.

courses.title: Social Media Marketing
courses.contact_hours: Credit Hours: 3, Lecture Hours: 3, Lab Hours: 0, Total Contact Hours: 3
courses.description: Surveys the use of social networks and online communities such as blogs, wikis, virtual events that allow companies to expand their interaction with customers and develop relationships with collaborative communities. Emphasizes the ongoing transformation of the way companies adjust their marketing plans to improve interaction with customers online.

courses.title: Introduction to Shipyard Trades
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week. 3 credits
courses.description: Provides an overview of shipyard trades and introduces core knowledge and safety practices common to all maritime occupations. Covers the use of hand and power tools, essential safety standards, and foundational skill sets aligned with specific trades.

courses.title: Shipyard Rigging Fundamentals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces fundamental rigging practices for shipyard environments, emphasizing safety, proper equipment usage, and effective communication during lifting operations. Covers basic principles of load dynamics, rigging hardware, and regulatory compliance. Designed to prepare students for entry-level rigging roles in maritime and industrial settings.

courses.title: Introduction to Ship Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces basic aspects of shipboard work, including: shipboard jobs, shipboard safety, ship classes, knot typing, ships nomenclatures, compartmentation, basic applied math skills, basic hand tools and working in confined spaces.

courses.title: Ship Plans and Systems Identification
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers essential skills and knowledge to read and interpret ship plans and identify standard compartmentation components and their labels/designations. Includes identifying various propulsion plant types and their respective application environments and classifying the predominant types of ships utilized in the commercial and military sectors.

courses.title: Shipyard Techniques, Construction and Overhaul Methods
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers essential shipyard techniques, safety measures, material strengths, welding and cutting skills, ship construction methods, and common fabrication processes. Includes fundamentals of ship construction methods and structures.

courses.title: Marine Maintenance Mechnaics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the various subjects comprising the study of mechanics to meet the unique requirements of marine practice. Includes basic nomenclature, construction and function of hulls, motive power principles, propellers, steering systems, controls, electrical equipment, instruments, and accessories.

courses.title: Basic Marine Electrical Circuits
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on basic electrical circuits common to small boat operations. Includes fundamentals of generators, alternators and their regulators, storage batteries, lighting systems instruments, protective devices, and all other primary power circuits, and the proper methods of installation, testing, trouble shooting, and repair.

courses.title: Introduction to Hydraulics and Hydraulics Systems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the fundamentals of basic symbols and diagrams of fluid power circuits. Includes control circuits from single motion to multiple interlocks, selection and use of common hydraulic components, operation and maintenance of shipboard pumps to include fuel transfer, raw water, fresh water, deck power, bilge and ballast, and sanitary electrical control of hydraulic circuits by switches, relays and solenoids.

courses.title: Small Outboard Engine Servcie
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the construction, theory of operation, maintenance and repair of small outboard motors. Includes modern diagnostic and test procedures, trouble shooting and repair followed by actual test tank operation.

courses.title: Inboard Engine Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on maintenance, repair and overhaul of modern gasoline inboard engines, drive components and stern drives. Stresses water diagnosis and test procedures.

courses.title: Large Outboard Engine Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the construction, theory of operation, maintenance and repair of larger outboard motors. Includes conventional D.C. battery charging systems and alternator theory, operation and maintenance, conventional and capacitive discharge ignition system, hydraulic system, modern diagnostic and test procedures, trouble shooting and repair followed by actual test tank operation.

courses.title: Stern Drive Transmission Service
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the fundamentals of stern drive marine propulsion units versus conventional shaft and propeller configurations. Stresses differences in shafting, bearings, lubrication, and steering. Includes proper methods of operation and maintenance; also minor and major repair operations to include complete disassembly, inspection and trouble-shooting and repair.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Marine Electronics for Maritime Vessels
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on theory of operation, service and repair of marine electronic systems. Includes control systems, navigation, RADAR, GPS, HF, VHF, satellite communications, lightning and corrosion protection systems.

courses.title: Studies In
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to assess the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Introduction to Army ROTC
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the first year of general military science: organization of the army and ROTC, U.S. Army and national security, individual weapons, marksmanship, and leadership laboratory. Courses offered only in cooperation with four- year colleges authorized to offer Army ROTC programs. Part I of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Leadership
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers the first year of general military science: organization of the army and ROTC, U.S. Army and national security, individual weapons, marksmanship, and leadership laboratory. Courses offered only in cooperation with four- year colleges authorized to offer Army ROTC programs. Part II of II.

courses.title: Sea Power and Maritime Affairs
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an in-depth assessment of the broad principles, concepts and elements of sea power with historical and modern applications to the United States and other world powers.

courses.title: Introduction to Naval Science
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction for midshipmen to the organization of the naval service, the varied career opportunities available, the long-held customs and traditions of the service, basic leadership, ethics and character development, the duties of a junior officer and Navy policies on wellness issues. Prepares NROTC midshipmen for their first experience onboard a Navy ship by imparting basic information concerning shipboard procedures and safety.

courses.title: Naval Science Laboratory I
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week. Co-requisite: MSC 125 and/or MSC 130 .
courses.description: Introduces basic military formations, drill movements, commands, customs, courtesies, honors and inspections. Covers applications of naval service concepts and principles in cruise preparation, shipboard safety, security, equal opportunity and military justice. First year Naval Science students only. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Leadership Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the second year of general military science: American military history, introduction to operations and basic tactics, map and aerial photo reading, and leadership laboratory. Courses offered only in cooperation with four- year colleges authorized to offer Army ROTC programs. Part I of II.

courses.title: Foundations of the Military Profession
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the second year of general military science: American military history, introduction to operations and basic tactics, map and aerial photo reading, and leadership laboratory. Courses offered only in cooperation with four- year colleges authorized to offer Army ROTC programs. Part II of II.

courses.title: Naval Ship Systems I: Naval Engineering
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an understanding of the physical properties and laws of thermodynamic systems, shipboard auxiliary systems, main propulsion, and electrical theory of shipboard power generation and distribution systems. Examines the criteria of ship design for seaworthiness, structural integrity and operational employment, the principles of fluid dynamics and shipboard safety.

courses.title: Naval Ship Systems II: Weapons
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an in-depth understanding of Naval Weapons, their associated systems, and the integration of these weapon systems into the overall naval strategy.

courses.title: Naval Science Laboratory II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week. Co-requisite: MSC 230 and/or MSC 231 .
courses.description: Builds on skills and knowledge of basic military formations, drill movements, commands, customs, courtesies, honors and inspections. Covers applications of naval service concepts and principles to ship design for seaworthiness, shipboard safety, systems administration, and naval strategy. Second year Naval Science students only. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: Basic Technical Mathematics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a foundation in mathematics with emphasis in arithmetic, unit conversion, basic algebra, geometry and trigonometry. This course is intended for CTE programs.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents elementary concepts of algebra, linear graphing, financial literacy, descriptive statistics, and measurement & geometry. Based on college programs being supported by this course, colleges may opt to add additional topics such as logic or trigonometry. This course is intended for occupational/technical programs.

courses.title: Technical Mathematics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents algebra through unit conversion, trigonometry, vectors, geometry, and complex numbers. This course is intended for CTE programs.

courses.title: Quantitative Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents topics in proportional reasoning, modeling, financial literacy and validity studies (logic and set theory). Focuses on the process of taking a real-world situation, identifying the mathematical foundation needed to address the problem, solving the problem and applying what is learned to the original situation. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Statistical Reasoning
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours, Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents elementary statistical methods and concepts including visual data presentation, descriptive statistics, probability, estimation, hypothesis testing, correlation and linear regression. Emphasis is placed on the development of statistical thinking, simulation, and the use of statistical software. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 155 : Statistical Reasoning and MTH 245 : Statistics I or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: PreCalculus I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents topics in power, polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, and systems of equations and inequalities. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 161 : Precalculus I and MTH 167 : Precalculus with Trigonometry or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: PreCalculus II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: Placement or completion of MTH 161 : Precalculus I or equivalent with a grade of C or better
courses.description: Presents trigonometry, trigonometric applications including Law of Sines and Cosines and an introduction to conics. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 162 : Precalculus II and MTH 167 : Precalculus with Trigonometry or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: PreCalculus with Trigonometry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 5 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents topics in power, polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, systems of equations, trigonometry, and trigonometric applications, including Law of Sines and Cosines, and an introduction to conics. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 167 : Precalculus with Trigonometry and MTH 161 /MTH 162: Precalculus I and II or equivalent. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Statistics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 154 or MTH 161 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Presents an overview of statistics, including descriptive statistics, elementary probability, probability distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, correlation, and linear regression. Credit will not be awarded for both MTH 155 and MTH 245 or equivalent in the same academic plan. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Applied Calculus I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 161 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Introduces limits, continuity, differentiation and integration of algebraic, exponential and logarithmic functions, and techniques of integration with an emphasis on applications in business, social sciences and life sciences. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Applied Calculus II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 261 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers techniques of integration, an introduction to differential equations and multivariable calculus, with an emphasis throughout on applications in business, social sciences and life sciences.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 167 or MTH 161 /162 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Presents concepts of limits, derivatives, differentiation of various types of functions and use of differentiation rules, application of differentiation, antiderivatives, integrals and applications of integration. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 263 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Continues the study of calculus of algebraic and transcendental functions including rectangular, polar, and parametric graphing, indefinite and definite integrals, methods of integration, and power series along with applications. Features instruction for mathematical, physical and engineering science programs. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Calculus III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 264 : Calculus II or equivalent with a grade of C or better
courses.description: Focuses on extending the concepts of function, limit, continuity, derivative, integral and vector from the plane to the three dimensional space. Covers topics including vector functions, multivariate functions, partial derivatives, multiple integrals and an introduction to vector calculus. Features instruction for mathematical, physical and engineering science programs.

courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 263 or equivalent with a grade of B or better or MTH 264 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers matrices, vector spaces, determinants, solutions of systems of linear equations, basis and dimension, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors. Features instruction for mathematical, physical and engineering science programs.

courses.title: Differential Equations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 264 or equivalent with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Introduces ordinary differential equations. Includes first order differential equations, second and higher order ordinary differential equations with applications and numerical methods.

courses.title: Probability and Statistics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 264 with a grade of C or better or equivalent.
courses.description: Presents basic concepts of probability, discrete and continuous random variables, and probability distributions. Presents sampling distributions and the Central Limit Theorem, properties of point estimates and methods of estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, linear models and estimation by least squares, and analysis of variance.

courses.title: Discrete Mathematics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 credits. Total 3 credits per week. Prerequisite: Completion of MTH 263 with a grade of C or better or equivalent.
courses.description: Presents topics in sets, counting, graphs, logic, proofs, functions, relations, mathematical induction, Boolean Algebra, and recurrence relations.

courses.title: Music Theory I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Discusses elements of musical construction of scales, intervals, triads, and chord progressions. Develops ability to sing at sight and write from dictation. Introduces the analysis of the Bach chorale style. Expands facility with harmonic dictation and enables the student to use these techniques at the keyboard. Part I of II.

courses.title: Music Theory II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Discusses elements of musical construction of scales, intervals, triads, and chord progressions. Develops ability to sing at sight and write from dictation. Introduces the analysis of the Bach chorale style. Expands facility with harmonic dictation and enables the student to use these techniques at the keyboard. Part II of II.

courses.title: Music in Society
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the language of music through an introduction to basic elements, forms and styles across time. Acquaints students with composers' lives and influential creative individualities, discovering representative works and milestones in western society. Develops techniques for listening analytically and critically. Reviews historical development and significance of art music within the context of evolving societal structures. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Jazz Ensemble
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0, Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Consists of performance from Standard Jazz and American Songbook Repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques, interpretation, and improvisation. Divisional approval required. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Applied Music-Voice
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches singing, proper breath control, diction, and development of tone. Studies the standard vocal repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. One or two half-hour lessons per week. Four to eight hours practice required.

courses.title: Chorus Ensemble
courses.contact_hours: Credits 1 - 2. Laboratory 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Ensemble consists of performance from the standard repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques and interpretation. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Class Piano I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers the beginning piano student activities in learning musical notation, in accomplishing sight reading skills, and in mastering techniques of keyboard playing. Presents appropriate literature. Open to all students and may be used to fulfill applied minor instrument requirement for music major. Part I of II.

courses.title: Class Piano II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers the beginning piano student activities in learning musical notation, in accomplishing sight reading skills, and in mastering techniques of keyboard playing. Presents appropriate literature. Open to all students and may be used to fulfill applied minor instrument requirement for music major. Part II of II.

courses.title: Applied Music - Keyboard
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches piano, organ, harpsichord, or synthesizer. Studies the standard repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. 1-2 half-hour lessons per week, 4-8 hours practice (laboratory) required.

courses.title: Orchestra Ensemble
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Ensemble consist of performance from the standard repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques and interpretation. Divisional approval required. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Applied Music - Woodwinds
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of the woodwind instruments. Studies the standard repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. 1-2 half-hour lessons per week, 4-8 hours practice (laboratory) required.

courses.title: Guitar Theory and Practice I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the fundamentals of sound production, music theory, and harmony as they apply to guitar. Builds proficiency in both the techniques of playing the guitar and in the application of music fundamentals to these techniques. Presents different types of guitars and related instruments. Emphasizes music as entertainment and as a communication skill. Part I of II.

courses.title: Applied Music - Strings
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of string instruments, harp, or guitar. Studies the standard repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. 1-2 half-hour lessons per week, 4-8 hours practice (laboratory) required.

courses.title: Applied Music - Brass
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of brass instruments. Studies the standard repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. 1-2 half-hour lessons per week, 4-8 hours practice (laboratory) required.

courses.title: Applied Music - Percussion
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Total 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals of percussion instruments. Studies the standard repertoire. Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. 1-2 half-hour lessons per week, 4-8 hours practice (laboratory) required.

courses.title: Advanced Music Theory I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: MUS 111 - MUS 112 or equivalent.
courses.description: Increases facility in the analysis and usage of diatonic and chromatic harmonies. Continues harmonic analysis of Bach style. Includes exercises in sight-singing, ear-training, and keyboard harmony. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Music Theory II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: MUS 111 -MUS 112 or equivalent.
courses.description: Increases facility in the analysis and usage of diatonic and chromatic harmonies. Continues harmonic analysis of Bach style. Includes exercises in sight-singing, ear-training, and keyboard harmony. Part II of II.

courses.title: History of Western Music Prior to 1750
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the chronology of musical styles and significant composers from Antiquity through the Pre-Classical era. Relates the development of music from a socio-historical perspective including parallel movements within the arts. Develops techniques for listening analytically and critically to music. MUS 221 and 222 may transfer as the same course. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: History of Western Music 1750 to Present
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the chronology of musical styles and significant composers from the Classical Period through the Modern era. Relates the development of music from a socio-historical perspective including parallel movements within the arts. Develops techniques for listening analytically and critically to music. MUS 221 and 222 may transfer as the same course. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Advanced Applied Music - Voice
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Prerequisite: Divisional approval required.
courses.description: Continues MUS 126 . Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. Laboratory 1-2 hours per week. & MUS 237 CHORUS (1 CR.) Continues MUS 137 . Courses in ensemble consist of performance from the standard repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques and interpretation. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Chorus Ensemble
courses.contact_hours: Credits 1 - 2. Laboratory 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Courses in ensemble consist of performance from the standard repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques and interpretation. May be repeated for credit. Continues MUS 137 .

courses.title: Advanced Jazz Ensemble
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0, Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Consists of performance from Standard Jazz and American Songbook Repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques, interpretation, and improvisation. Divisional approval and completion of Jazz Ensemble required. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Advanced Class Piano I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches advanced applications of keyboard fundamentals and technical skills. Includes exercises in intervals, triads, all major and minor scales, and simple and compound meters. Uses advanced repertoire. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Class Piano II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches advanced applications of keyboard fundamentals and technical skills. Includes exercises in intervals, triads, all major and minor scales, and simple and compound meters. Uses advanced repertoire. Part II of II.

courses.title: Advanced Applied Music - Keyboard
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues Applied Music - Keyboard MUS 145 . Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor.

courses.title: Orchestra
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Ensemble consist of performance from the standard repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques and interpretation. Divisional approval required. May be repeated for credit. Continues MUS 148 .

courses.title: Advanced Applied Music - Woodwinds
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues Applied Music - Woodwinds MUS 155 . Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor.

courses.title: Advanced Applied Music - Strings
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues Applied Music - Strings MUS 165 . Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor.

courses.title: Advanced Applied Music - Brass
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Divisional approval required.
courses.description: Continues Applied Music Brass MUS 175 . Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. Laboratory 1-2 hours per week. & MUS 276 BRASS ENSEMBLE (1 CR.) Continues Brass Ensemble MUS 176 . Courses in ensemble consist of performance from the standard repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques and interpretation. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Advanced Applied Music - Percussion
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 4-8 hours per week. Divisional approval required.
courses.description: Continues Applied Music - Percussion MUS 185 . Private lessons are available for either 1 or 2 hours of credit per semester. The length of the lessons will be 1/2 hour for 1 hour credit and 1 hour for 2 hours credit per semester. All courses in applied music may be repeated for a total of 8 hours for the major and 4 hours for the minor. Laboratory 1-2 hours per week. & MUS 286 PERCUSSION ENSEMBLE (1 CR.) Continues Percussion Ensemble MUS 186 . Courses in ensemble consist of performance from the standard repertoires, including study of ensemble techniques and interpretation. May be repeated for credit.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Science in the Workplace
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores concepts of basic physical sciences as they apply to the workplace. Presents scientific methods, energy, heat, and temperature as related to various materials used in the workplace. Designed for trade workers that work with a variety of materials in many different applications. Assists workers with the physical properties of materials as they relate to various manufacturing methods.

courses.title: Meteorology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Recitation and laboratory 2 hours per week. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents a non-technical survey of fundamentals meteorology. Focuses on the effects of weather and climate on humans and their activities. Serves for endorsement or recertification of earth science teachers.

courses.title: Elements of Astronomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Recitation and laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers history of astronomy and its recent developments. Stresses the use of astronomical instruments and measuring techniques and includes the study and observation of the solar system, stars, and galaxies.

courses.title: Astronomy: Solar System
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces astronomy of the solar system, including the Sun, planets, their satellites, and other solar system objects. Includes discussions of the development of astronomy through the ages, recent discoveries, and experience with the types of mathematical exercises and observational skills essential for an understanding of the fundamental principles of solar system astronomy. Assignments require fluency in arithmetic, unit conversion, basic algebra, geometry, and trigonometry. This course is cross-listed with PHY 141 . Credit will not be awarded for both.

courses.title: Astronomy: Stars and Galaxies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces astronomy of the stars, including the Sun, celestial objects, stellar formation and death and cosmology, and the study of the universe as a whole. Includes discussions of the development of astronomy through the ages, recent discoveries and experience with the types of mathematical principles employed and the astronomical observational skills essential for an understanding of the fundamental principles of astronomy and cosmology. Assignments require fluency in arithmetic, unit conversion, basic algebra, geometry, and trigonometry. This course is cross-listed with PHY 142 . Credit will not be awarded for both.

courses.title: Upper Extremity Anatomy and Kinesiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hour per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the upper extremity anatomy to include the entire shoulder girdle and the impact of pathology and injury related to the skeletal, nervous and muscular systems. Covers planes of movement of the upper extremity associated with basic physics and types of levers.

courses.title: Introduction to Nursing Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 141 or BIO 231
courses.description: Introduces concepts of nursing practice and conceptual learning. Focuses on basic nursing concepts with an emphasis on safe nursing practice and the development of the nursing process. Provides supervised learning experiences in college nursing laboratories, clinical/community settings, and/or simulated environments.

courses.title: Competencies for Nursing Practice
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hour. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 4-6 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 141 (or BIO 231 )
courses.description: Focuses on the application of concepts through clinical skill development. Emphasizes the use of clinical judgment in skill acquisition. Includes principles of safety, evidence-based practice, informatics and math computational skills. Prepares students to demonstrate competency in specific skills and drug dosage calculation including the integration of skills in the care of clients in simulated settings. Provides supervised learning experiences in college nursing laboratories, clinical/community settings, and/or simulated environments.

courses.title: Healthcare Concepts for Transition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 6-9 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 141 , BIO 142 , ENG 111 , PSY 230 , SDV 100 ; Acceptance to the Transition Program. Corequisite: NSG 200 .
courses.description: Focuses on role transition from Licensed Practical Nurse to Registered professional nurse. Incorporates concepts of nursing practice and conceptual learning to promote health and wellness across the lifespan. Uses the nursing process to explore care delivery for selected diverse populations with common and predictable illness. Emphasizes the use of clinical judgement in skill acquisition.

courses.title: Concepts for Health Professions Transition
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 8 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 141 and acceptance into the AAS Nursing Program - Paramedic/Registered Respiratory Therapist to RN. Corequisites: BIO 142 , NSG 130 and NSG 200 .
courses.description: Facilitates role transition for the Paramedic or Respiratory Therapist to Registered Nurse. Incorporates concepts of nursing practice and conceptual learning focusing on basic nursing concepts with an emphasis on safe nursing practice. Includes the development of the nursing process. Emphasizes the use of clinical judgement in skill acquisition. Provides supervised learning experiences in college nursing laboratories, clinical/community settings, and/or simulated environments.

courses.title: Professional Nursing Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Total 1 hour per week. Prerequisites: BIO 141 or BIO 231
courses.description: Introduces the role of the professional nurse and fundamental concepts in professional development. Focuses on professional identity, legal/ethical issues and contemporary trends in professional nursing.

courses.title: Health Care Participant
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 142 (or BIO 232 ), NSG 100 , NSG 106 , NSG 130 and NSG 200
courses.description: Focuses on the health and wellness of diverse individuals, families, and the community throughout the lifespan. Covers concepts that focus on client attributes and preferences regarding healthcare. Emphasizes population-focused care. Provides supervised learning experiences in college nursing laboratories, clinical/community settings, and/or cooperating agencies, and/or simulated environments.

courses.title: Health/Illness Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours, Laboratory 6 hours. Total 10 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 142 (or BIO 232 ), NSG 100 , NSG 106 , NSG 130 and NSG 200
courses.description: Focuses on the nursing care of individuals and/or families throughout the lifespan with an emphasis on health and illness concepts. Includes concepts of nursing care for the antepartum client and clients with common and predictable illnesses. Provides supervised learning experiences in college nursing laboratories, clinical/community settings, and/or simulated environments.

courses.title: Health Promotion and Assessment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 141 (or BIO 231 )
courses.description: Introduces assessment and health promotion for the individual and family. Includes assessment of infants, children, adults, geriatric clients and pregnant females. Emphasizes health history and the acquisition of physical assessment skills with underlying concepts of development, communication, and health promotion. Prepares students to demonstrate competency in the assessment of clients across the lifespan. Provides supervised learning experiences in college nursing laboratories, clinical/community settings, and/or simulated environments.

courses.title: Health Care Concepts I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours, Laboratory 6 hours. Total 9 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 150 (or BIO 205 ), NSG 152 and NSG 170
courses.description: Focuses on care of clients across the lifespan in multiple settings including concepts related to physiological health alterations and reproduction. Emphasizes the nursing process in the development of clinical judgment for clients with multiple needs. Provides supervised learning experiences in college nursing laboratories, clinical/community settings, and/or simulated environments. Part I of II.

courses.title: Health Care Concepts II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 6 hours. Total 9 hours per week. Prerequisites: BIO 150 (or BIO 205 ), NSG 152 and NSG 170
courses.description: Focuses on care of clients across the lifespan in multiple settings including concepts related to psychological and physiological health alterations. Emphasizes the nursing process in the development of clinical judgment for clients with multiple needs. Provides supervised learning experiences in college nursing laboratories, clinical/community settings, and/or simulated environments. Part II of II.

courses.title: Advanced Professional Nursing Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisites: NSG 210 and NSG 211
courses.description: Develops the role of the professional nurse in the healthcare environment in preparation for practice as a registered nurse. Introduces leadership and management concepts and focuses on the integration of professional behaviors in a variety of healthcare settings.

courses.title: Complex Health Care Concepts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisites: NSG 210 and NSG 211
courses.description: Focuses on nursing care of diverse individuals and families integrating complex health concepts. Emphasizes clinical judgment, patient-centered care and collaboration.

courses.title: Nursing Capstone
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 12 hours. Total 12 hours per week. Prerequisites: NSG 210 and NSG 211
courses.description: Provides students with the opportunity to comprehensively apply and integrate learned concepts from previous nursing courses into a capstone experience. Emphasizes the mastery of patient- centered care, safety, nursing judgment, professional behaviors, informatics, quality improvement, and collaboration in the achievement of optimal outcomes of care. Provides supervised learning experiences in faculty and/or preceptor-guided college nursing laboratories, clinical/community settings, and/or simulated environments.

courses.title: Clinical Reasoning in Current Nursing Practice
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. 2 Credits.
courses.description: Discusses clinical reasoning and the critical thinking process used in nursing. Incorporates practical reasoning, which complements the scientific reasoning used in the nursing process. Forms the basis for the thinking process applied throughout all nursing courses.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Introduction to Occupational Therapy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the concepts of occupational therapy as a means of directing a person's participation in tasks selected to develop, maintain or restore skills in daily living. Examines the role of the assistant for each function of occupational therapy, and for various practice settings in relationship to various members of the health care team.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Occupational Therapy With Psychosocial Dysfunction
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the theory and application of occupational therapy in the evaluation and treatment of psychosocial dysfunction. Includes a survey of conditions which cause emotional, mental and social disability, as well as the role of the occupational therapy assistant in the assessment, planning and implementation of treatment programs.

courses.title: Occupational Therapy With Physical Disabilities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the theory and application of occupational therapy in the evaluation and treatment of physical dysfunction. Includes a survey of conditions which cause physical disability as well as the role of the occupational therapy assistant in assessment, planning and implementation of treatment programs.

courses.title: Occupational Therapy with Developmental Disabilities
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the theory and application of occupational therapy in the evaluation and treatment of developmental dysfunction. Includes a survey of conditions which cause developmental disability across the life span, with particular emphasis on children and the elderly. Investigates the role of the occupational therapist in assessment, planning and implementation of treatment programs.

courses.title: Therapeutic Media
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per
courses.description: Develops proficiency in various crafts used as treatment modalities in occupational therapy. Emphasizes how to analyze, adapt and teach selected activities as well as how to equip and maintain a safe working environment.

courses.title: Dyadic and Group Dynamics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides theory and activity to develop positive interpersonal relationships and effective communication ability. Includes non-verbal communication, listening, observation, interviewing and documentation. Covers group process and its application to occupational therapy, including types of therapeutic groups, group membership roles, leadership skills and forces which affect group function and decision making.

courses.title: Therapeutic Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents techniques used in the treatment of a variety of conditions frequently seen across the life span. Emphasizes the activities of self-care, work, and leisure as they relate to the development/resumption of normal social role functioning.

courses.title: Occupational Therapy Service Management
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents principles and techniques of management appropriate to the occupational therapy assistant. Includes roles and functions of the supervisor and the supervisee, scheduling, billing, quality improvement. Issues relevant to professional practice and patient care will be discussed with similarities and differences between various facilities highlighted.

courses.title: Assistive Technology in Occupational Therapy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Explores the assistive technologies available for persons with physical, sensory and cognitive disabilities. Provides instruction in the process of assessment, selection adaptation and training of assistive technology to persons with disability. Presents information on funding and maintenance of devices. Exposes students to technology in clinical practice and equipment companies.

courses.title: Occupational Therapy for the Adult
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Reviews normal changes related to aging and factors contributing to dysfunction. Analyzes intervention strategies for common problems, including wellness programs and home modifications. Reviews relevant legislation, continuum of care and caregiver issues.

courses.title: Neurological Concepts for Occupational Therapy Assistants
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the workings of the human nervous system from the cellular level to the systems level with an emphasis on normal neurological function, the impact of neurological dysfunction, and how to use neurological rehabilitation techniques to facilitate the rehabilitation process across the lifespan.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Interviewing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Analyzes the principles and techniques of interviewing in various organizational settings. Examines reliability and validity of information gained through information interviewing, employment and selection interviewing, performance appraisal and disciplinary interviewing, as well as counseling interviewing.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Physical Activity I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents principles underlying the components of physical fitness. Utilizes conditioning activities involving cardiovascular strength and endurance, respiratory efficiency, muscular strength, and flexibility. May include fitness assessment, nutrition and weight control information, and concepts of wellness. Part I of II.

courses.title: Exercise and Nutrition I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides for the study and application of fitness and wellness and their relationship to a healthy lifestyle. Defines fitness and wellness, evaluates the student's level of fitness and wellness. Students will incorporate physical fitness and wellness into the course and daily living. A personal fitness/wellness plan is required for the 2 credit course. Part I of II.

courses.title: Yoga
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the forms of yoga training emphasizing flexibility.

courses.title: Weight Training I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on muscular strength and endurance training through individualized workout programs. Teaches appropriate use of weight training equipment. Part I of II.

courses.title: Fitness Walking
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches content and skills needed to design, implement, and evaluate an individualized program of walking, based upon fitness level.

courses.title: Self-Defense
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 2-4 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines history, techniques, and movements associated with self-defense. Introduces the skills and methods of self- defense emphasizing mental and physical discipline.

courses.title: Basic Personal Trainer Preparation
courses.contact_hours: 3 credit hours. 2 lecture hours. 2 lab hours. 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the skills and knowledge required to become a personal trainer. Includes the principles of individual weight management, personal wellness, and the skills necessary for the creation of a fitness program for potential clients.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents an introduction to philosophical problems and perspectives with emphasis on the systematic questioning of basic assumptions about meaning, knowledge, reality, and values. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Logic
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces inductive and deductive reasoning, with an emphasis on common errors and fallacies. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Ethics and Society
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides a systematic study of representative ethical concepts and theories and discusses their application to concrete moral dilemmas and social issues and problems. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: History of Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys important photographers, processes, and historical influences of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

courses.title: Introduction to Digital Photography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
