courses.description: Introduces fundamental techniques of photography, including digital camera operation, postproduction, and printing. Includes technical and conceptual exercises, individual project development, and group critiques.

courses.title: Imaging and Concepts in Photographic Media Arts
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 4 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers best practices in imaging workflows, concept building, ideation, and steps in the creative process. Introduces students to working with multiple images in a series and as sequence. Provides students the opportunity to create and manipulate digital images and examine property-rights issues. Exposes students to a variety of software used for image organization, archiving, image editing, compositing, layer masking, the application of special effects, and outsourcing.

courses.title: Advanced Photography I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHT 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Provides weekly critiques of students' work. Centers on specific problems found in critiques. Includes working procedures and critical skills in looking at photographs. Part I of II.

courses.title: Studio Lighting I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines advanced lighting and camera techniques under controlled studio conditions. Includes view camera use, electronic flash, advanced lighting techniques, color temperature and filtration, and lighting ratios. Requires outside shooting. Part I of II.

courses.title: Studio Lighting II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHT 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Examines advanced lighting and camera techniques under controlled studio conditions. Includes view camera use, electronic flash, advanced lighting techniques, color temperature and filtration, and lighting ratios. Requires outside shooting. Part II of II.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Elements of Physics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Covers basic concepts of physics, including Newtonian mechanics, properties of matter, heat transfer, waves, fundamental behavior of gases, optics, ionizing radiation, and fundamentals of electricity and magnetism. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency, coherent written communication, application of arithmetic, exponents, and algebraic skills such as solving for an unknown variable in an equation, and finding the slope and intercept from the equation of a line. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Topics In
courses.contact_hours: May be used also for special honors courses. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Provides an opportunity to explore topical areas of interest to or needed by students.

courses.title: General College Physics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: MTH 161 or MTH 167 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers classical mechanics and thermodynamics. Includes kinematics, Newton's laws of motion, work, energy, momentum, rotational kinematics, dynamic and static equilibrium, elasticity, gravitation, fluids, simple harmonic motion, calorimetry, ideal gas law, and the laws of thermodynamics. Part I of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: General College Physics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: PHY 201 with a grade of C or better and MTH 162 or MTH 167 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers waves, electromagnetism, optics, and modern physics. Includes mechanical waves, sound, electrostatics, Ohm's law and DC circuits, magnetic forces and magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, ray optics, wave optics, and selected topics of modern physics. Part II of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: University Physics I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: MTH 263 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers classical mechanics and thermodynamics. Includes kinematics, Newton's laws of motion, work, energy, momentum, rotational kinematics, dynamics and static equilibrium, elasticity, gravitation, fluids, simple harmonic motion, calorimetry, ideal gas law, and the laws of thermodynamics. Part I of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: University Physics II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisites: PHY 241 with a grade of C or better and MTH 264 with a grade of C or better.
courses.description: Covers waves, electromagnetism and optics. Includes mechanical waves and sound, electrostatics, Ohm's law and DC circuits, magnetic forces and magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, AC circuits, ray optics, and wave optics. Part II of II. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: U.S. Government and Politics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches the political structure, processes, institutions, and policymaking of the US national government. Focuses on the three branches of government, their interrelationships, and how they shape policy. Addresses federalism; civil liberties and civil rights; political socialization and participation; public opinion, the media; interest groups; political parties; elections; and policymaking. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: State and Local Government and Politics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches structure, powers, and functions of state and local government in the United States as related to federalism; constitutionalism; elections; powers of legislative, executive, and judicial powers of state and local government; state-local-federal relations; fiscal matters; metropolitan issues; and policy issues, like health, education, criminal justice and welfare. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports.

courses.title: Introduction to Comparative Politics
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teach concepts and methods of comparative politics. Includes empirical analyses of domestic governmental, political, and societal institutions and norms of countries around the world. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Introduction to International Relations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: ENG 111 or Department Consent
courses.description: Provides an introduction to the causes of international conflict and cooperation. Focuses on the modern state, diplomacy, war initiation, crisis bargaining, international terrorism, nuclear strategy, interstate economic relations, economic growth, international law, human rights, and environmental politics. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Trends in Practical Nursing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Studies the role of the Licensed Practical Nurse. Covers legal aspects, organizations, and opportunities in practical nursing. Assists students in preparation for employment.

courses.title: Mental Health and Psychiatric Nursing
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Recognizes emotional needs of patients. Provides knowledge of the role that emotions play. Enables students to understand their own behavior as well as patient behavior.

courses.title: Nursing in Health Changes II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-6 hours. Laboratory 12-21 hours. Total 18-25 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues the focus on nursing situations and procedures necessary to assist individuals in meeting special needs related to human functions.

courses.title: Nursing in Health Changes III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-5 hours. Laboratory 9-15 hours. Total 14-19 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues the focus on nursing situations and procedures necessary to assist individuals in meeting special needs related to human functions.

courses.title: Nursing in Health Changes IV
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4-6 hours. Laboratory 12-21 hours. Total 18-25 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues the focus on nursing situations and procedures necessary to assist individuals in meeting special needs related to human functions.

courses.title: Applied Pharmacology for Practical Nurses
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 0-1 hour. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 3-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Applies problem solving skills in preparing and administering medications.

courses.title: Psychology of Death and Dying
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on psychological aspects of death and dying. Teaches the meaning of death and ways of handling its personal and social implications. Includes psychological, sociological, cultural, and religious views of death.

courses.title: Psychology for Business and Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the application of psychology to interpersonal relations and the working environment. Includes topics such as group dynamics, motivation, employee-employer relationship, interpersonal communications. May include techniques for selection and supervision of personnel.

courses.title: Principles of Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the basic concepts of psychology. Covers the scientific study of behavior and mental processes, research methods, biological bases of behavior, sensation and perception, developmental psychology, learning, memory, thinking, intelligence, personality, social psychology, and psychological disorders and treatment. The assignments in the course require college-level reading fluency and coherent communication through written reports. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Psychopathology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: PSY 200 or departmental approval.
courses.description: Explores historical views and current perspectives of psychopathology. Emphasizes major diagnostic categories and criteria, individual and social factors of maladaptive behavior, and types of treatments. Includes methods of clinical assessment and research strategies.

courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: PSY 200 or departmental consent.
courses.description: Examines individuals in social contexts, their social roles, group processes and intergroup relations. Acquaints students with a scientific understanding of how the presence of other people, interactions with other people, and other situational factors influence human thoughts and behaviors. The assignments in the course require college-level reading, analysis of scholarly studies, and coherent communication through written reports (including the production of at least one APA-formatted individual writing assignment).

courses.title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the systematic study of behavior and experience as it occurs in different cultures. Covers the interaction and interpretation of culture and development, self and identity, personality, gender, cognition, emotion, communication, physical health, mental health, and social behavior.

courses.title: Theories of Personality
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: PSY 200 or equivalent
courses.description: Studies the major personality theories and their applications. Includes psychodynamic, behavioral, cognitive, and humanistic perspectives.

courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Traces development in context from pre-conception to death, including the physical, cognitive, and psychosocial domains. Examines methods of scientific inquiry as they apply to lifespan development. Addresses the interrelatedness of developmental domains, as well as the interdependent influences of environment and biology. Students majoring in or considering a major in Psychology should complete PSY 200 prior to PSY 230 .

courses.title: Life Span Human Development I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates human behavior through the life cycle. Describes physical, cognitive, and psycho-social aspects of human development from conception to death. Part I of II.

courses.title: Life Span Human Development II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Investigates human behavior through the life cycle. Describes physical, cognitive, and psycho-social aspects of human development from conception to death. Part II of II.

courses.title: Child Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies development of the child from conception to adolescence. Investigates physical, intellectual, social and emotional factors involved in the child's growth.

courses.title: Psychological Aspects of Criminal Behavior
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: PSY 125 , PSY 200 , PSY 201 , PSY 202 or divisional approval.
courses.description: Studies psychology of criminal behavior. Includes topics such as violent and non-violent crime, sexual offenses, insanity, addiction, white collar crime, and other deviant behaviors. Provides a background for law enforcement occupations.

courses.title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisites: PSY 200 , PSY 201 or PSY 202 .
courses.description: Focuses on scientific investigation of human sexuality and psychological and social implications of such research. Considers socio-cultural influences, the physiology and psychology of sexual response patterns, sexual dysfunctions, and development of relationships.

courses.title: Introduction to Physical Therapist Assisting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2-4 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the physical therapist assistant student to the field of physical therapy practice and develops basic patient care skills for application in the initial physical therapy clinical experience.

courses.title: Medical Reporting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes the principles of medical reporting, including the ability to abstract pertinent information from actual medical records. Includes the writing of patient progress notes in standardized formats and medical terminology.

courses.title: Kinesiology for the Physical Therapist Assistant
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the relationship of specific joint structure and function, the role of individual muscles and groups of muscles and neurologic principles in both normal and pathological movement. The course includes a review of basic physics and biomechanical principles applied to human movement. Includes specific posture and gait analysis.

courses.title: Therapeutic Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 4-6 hours. Total 7-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares the students to properly and safely administer basic physical therapy procedures utilized by physical therapist assistants. The procedures include therapeutic modalities. Procedures may include therapeutic exercise, electrotherapy and cardiopulmonary rehabilitation. Part I of II.

courses.title: Therapeutic Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 4-6 hours. Total 7-9 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares the students to properly and safely administer basic physical therapy procedures utilized by physical therapist assistants. The procedures include therapeutic modalities. Procedures may include therapeutic exercise, electrotherapy and cardiopulmonary rehabilitation. Part II of II.

courses.title: Clinical Education
courses.contact_hours: Lcture 0-1 hours. Laboratory 4-15 hours. Total 5-15 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides supervised instruction in the delivery of physical therapy in one of various clinical settings. Emphasizes the practice of all therapeutic skills learned in the first year, including direct patient care skills and all forms of communication.

courses.title: Musculoskeletal Structure and Function
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies the human musculoskeletal system. Covers terms of position and movement, location and identification of specific bony landmarks, joint structure and design, ligaments, muscle origin, action and innervation, and emphasizes types of contraction.

courses.title: Psychological Aspects of Therapy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the psychological reactions and sociological impact of illness and injury in clients and their families, and among health care givers who work with them. Examines individual self-identity and the nature of changing client/ therapist relationships across the life span.

courses.title: Rehabilitation Procedures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-9 hours. Total 5-11 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on treatment techniques typical of long term rehabilitation, e.g., the rehabilitation of congenital, neurological and disfigurement associated with chronic injury and disease.

courses.title: Therapeutic Exercise
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 2-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Emphasizes the basic principles underlying different approaches to exercise including rationale for treatment and may include neurological treatments such a simple facilitation and inhibitory techniques and the teaching of home programs.

courses.title: Pathological Conditions
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents specific pathologic conditions commonly seen in physical therapy. Emphasizes musculoskeletal and neurological system conditions, and all major body systems are represented.

courses.title: Clinical Practicum I
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 15-20 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in local health care facilities in the actual administration of physical therapy treatments under the supervision of licensed physical therapists. Provides experience in a variety of clinical settings. Part I of II.

courses.title: Clinical Practicum II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 15-20 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides instruction in local health care facilities in the actual administration of physical therapy treatments under the supervision of licensed physical therapists. Provides experience in a variety of clinical settings. Part II of II.

courses.title: Seminar in Physical Therapy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes preparation for licensing examination, specialized lectures, and preparation of a student project.

courses.title: Principles of Magnetic Resonance Imaging
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Presents concepts of Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Physics. Teaches fundamentals of Magnetic Resonance and application of principles.

courses.title: Medical Care Procedures & Safety in Radiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite-Corequisite: Admission to RAD Program.
courses.description: Teaches the fundamentals of radiation safety, body mechanics and medical legal considerations in Radiology. Presents techniques of infection control, patient care safety, and response to emergency situations. Introduces pharmacology, contrast media, and treatment of adverse reactions. Students acquire skills in vital sign assessment, sterile technique, venipuncture, and other medical care procedures.

courses.title: Radiographic Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces procedures for positioning the patient's anatomical structures relative to X-ray beam and image receptor. Emphasizes procedures for routine examination of the chest, abdomen, extremities, and axial skeleton.

courses.title: Elementary Clinical Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 15 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops advanced technical skills in fundamental radiographic procedures. Focuses on manipulation of equipment, patient care, osseous studies, skull procedures, and contrast studies. Provides clinical experience in cooperating health agencies. Part I of II.

courses.title: Elementary Clinical Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 15 hours per week.
courses.description: Develops advanced technical skills in fundamental radiographic procedures. Focuses on manipulation of equipment, patient care, osseous studies, skull procedures, and contrast studies. Provides clinical experience in cooperating health agencies. Part II of II.

courses.title: Principles of Radiographic Quality I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Admission to Program.
courses.description: Presents factors that control and influence radiographic quality, as well as, various technical conversion factors useful in radiography. Discusses automatic film processing, sensitometry, and quality assurance testing. Part I of II.

courses.title: Principles of Radiographic Quality II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: Admission to Program.
courses.description: Presents factors that control and influence radiographic quality, as well as, various technical conversion factors useful in radiography. Discusses automatic film processing, sensitometry, and quality assurance testing. Part II of II.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Studies In
courses.contact_hours: Variable hours per week.
courses.description: Covers new content not covered in existing courses in the discipline. Allows instructor to explore content and instructional methods to assess the course's viability as a permanent offering.

courses.title: On-Site Training
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Specializes in career orientation and training program without pay in selected businesses and industry, supervised and coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Radiation Protection and Radiobiology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies methods and devices used for protection from ionizing radiation. Teaches theories of biological effects, cell and organism sensitivity, and the somatic and genetic effects of ionizing radiation. Presents current radiation protection philosophy for protecting the patient and technologist.

courses.title: Human Disease and Radiography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the various diseases and anomalies that may be manifested on the radiograph. Presents diseases related to the various body systems. Places emphasis on the relationship of the disease process and radiographic density.

courses.title: Radiographic Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues procedures for positioning the patient's anatomical structures relative to X-ray beam and image receptor. Emphasizes procedures for routine examination of the skull, contrast studies of internal organs, and special procedures employed in the more complicated investigation of the human body.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 20-25 hours per week.
courses.description: Reinforces technical skills in fundamental radiographic procedures. Introduces more intricate contrast media procedures. Focuses on technical proficiency, application of radiation, protection, nursing skills, and exposure principles. Teaches advanced technical procedures and principles of imaging modalities, correlating previous radiographic theory, focusing on full responsibility for patients in technical areas, perfecting technical skills, and developing awareness of related areas utilizing ionizing radiation. Provides clinical experience in cooperating health agencies. Part I of II.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 20-25 hours per week.
courses.description: Reinforces technical skills in fundamental radiographic procedures. Introduces more intricate contrast media procedures. Focuses on technical proficiency, application of radiation, protection, nursing skills, and exposure principles. Teaches advanced technical procedures and principles of imaging modalities, correlating previous radiographic theory, focusing on full responsibility for patients in technical areas, perfecting technical skills, and developing awareness of related areas utilizing ionizing radiation. Provides clinical experience in cooperating health agencies. Part II of II.

courses.title: Anatomy and Positioning of the Breast
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Presents the risk factors for breast disease, anatomy and physiology of the breast and discusses the various pathologies identified through mammography. Includes routine and special projections of the breast.

courses.title: Breast Imaging/Instrumentation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Discusses the dedicated radiography equipment necessary for breast imaging. Includes proper technical factors, radiation protection techniques, and proper accessory equipment.

courses.title: Quality Assurance in Mammography
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Discusses the components of quality assurance in mammography and the accreditation programs developed to ensure quality in breast imaging facilities.

courses.title: Computed Tomography Procedures and Instrumentation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Focuses on the patient care, imaging procedure and physics and instrumentation related to computed tomography imaging.

courses.title: Radiologic Specialties
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the study of treatment of disease as it relates to various imaging modalities, computerized tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging. Introduces computers and other innovations in radiology. Emphasizes theory, principle of operation, and clinical application of these topics.

courses.title: Cross-Sectional Anatomy
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Presents a specialized study of cross-sectional anatomy relevant to sectional imaging modalities such as computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging.

courses.title: Case Studies in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MR)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ARRT or eligible.
courses.description: Introduces student to role of collaborator in patient care by providing the critical thinking skills necessary to implement appropriate examination protocols and patient care essential for obtaining diagnostic images. Features cases that can be performed via Magnetic Resonance (MR) simulation or from actual MR examinations.

courses.title: Radiographic Equipment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies principles and operation of general and specialized X-ray equipment.

courses.title: Terminal Competencies in Radiography
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 3 hours per week. Prerequisite/Co-requisite: Admission to RAD program.
courses.description: Includes preparation and ensures that students possess competencies which relate to materials covered by the ARRT Content Specifications for national exam eligibility. Incorporates activities designed to verify that students have mastered skills in the critical content areas to include equipment operation and maintenance, image production and evaluation, radiographic procedures, radiation protection and patient care.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: On-Site Training
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Specializes in career orientation and training program without pay in selected businesses and industry, supervised and coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Supervised Study
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Assigns problems for independent study incorporating previous instruction and supervised by the instructor.

courses.title: Religions of the World
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the major religions of the world: Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, and Buddhism. Focuses on origins, history, basic beliefs, values, ethics, and practices. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Integrated Sciences for Respiratory Care II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Integrates the concepts of mathematics, chemistry, physics, microbiology, and computer technology as these sciences apply to the practices of respiratory care.

courses.title: Fundamental Theory for Respiratory Care
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the theory of basic patient assessment and functional medical terminology.

courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Science I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on pathophysiology, assessment, treatment, and evaluation of patients with cardiopulmonary disease. Explores cardiopulmonary and neuromuscular physiology and patho- physiology.

courses.title: Respiratory Care Theory and Procedures I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents theory of equipment and procedures and related concepts used for patients requiring general, acute and critical cardiopulmonary care. Part I of II.

courses.title: Respiratory Care Theory and Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents theory of equipment and procedures and related concepts used for patients requiring general, acute and critical cardiopulmonary care. Part II of II.

courses.title: Pharmacology for Respiratory Care I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents selection criteria for the use of, and detailed information on pharmacologic agents used in pulmonary care.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: On-Site Training
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Specializes in career orientation and training program without pay in selected businesses and industry, supervised and coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Pulmonary Rehab., Home Care and Health Promotion
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on purpose and implementation of a comprehensive pulmonary rehabilitation program. Explores procedures and approaches used in pulmonary home care. Identifies and discusses major health and wellness programs applied to cardiopulmonary patients.

courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Science II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on assessment, treatment, and evaluation of patients with cardiopulmonary disease. Explores cardiopulmonary, renal, and neuromuscular physiology, and pathophysiology.

courses.title: Cardiopulmonary Science III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues the exploration of topics discussed in RTH 121 and 222.

courses.title: Neonatal and Pediatric Respiratory Procedures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the cardiopulmonary, physiology, pathology and application of therapeutic procedures in the management of the newborn and pediatric patient.

courses.title: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Procedures II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the use of multiple diagnostic and therapeutic techniques used in ambulatory and critical care patients.

courses.title: Critical Care Monitoring
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on techniques and theory necessary for the evaluation and treatment of the critical care patient, especially arterial blood gases and hemodynamic measurements. Explores physiologic effects of advanced mechanical ventilation.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Procedures III
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 15-20 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers clinical instruction in advanced patient care practices.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Procedures IV
courses.contact_hours: Clinical 15-20 hours per week.
courses.description: Offers clinical instruction in advanced patient care practice.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Beginning Russian I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Russian II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisites: RUS 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school Russian, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Develops the understanding, speaking, reading, and writing of Russian, and emphasizes the structure of the language. May include oral drill and practice. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Russian I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: RUS 102 , or three years of successful completion of high school Russian, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and introduces complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in target language. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Russian II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: RUS 201 , or four years of successful completion of high school Russian, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in the target language. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Safety & Health Standards: Regulations and Codes
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches development of safety standards, the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA), its rules and regulations; penalties for non-compliance, and methods of compliance. Includes an examination of Government Regulatory Codes and appraisal of consensus, advisory, and proprietary standards.

courses.title: Principles of Industrial Safety
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches principles and practices of accident prevention, analysis of accident causes, mechanical safeguards, fire prevention, housekeeping, occupational diseases, first aid, safety organization, protection equipment and general safety principles and promotion.

courses.title: Industrial Safety - OSHA 10
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Presents an introduction to occupational health and safety and its application in the workplace. Emphasizes safety standards and the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA), its rules and regulations (OSHA 10).

courses.title: Safety Program Organization and Administration
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces techniques of organizing and administering practical safety programs. Emphasizes safety as a management function. Includes an examination of history, occupational safety and health regulations, and a survey of current laws, codes and standards.

courses.title: Working at Heights and Safety Procedures
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 2 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches how to properly use basic personal protective equipment and how to perform manual handling tasks in a safe manner in the wind turbine industry/environment. Includes appropriate alternatives to manual handling through planning.

courses.title: Human Factors & Safety Psychology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies stresses on the human system, both physiological and psychological, that contribute to the severity of industrial accidents. Includes the interrelationship of industrial medicine and industrial hygiene and a study of the various occupational illnesses.

courses.title: Hazardous Chemicals, Materials, and Waste in the Workpl
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the rules and regulations governing use, exposure to, and disposal of hazardous chemicals, materials and waste by-products. Discusses OSHA "Right to Know Laws," EPA and RCRA regulations. Provides the techniques to interpret and understand the code of Federal Regulations. Emphasis on management mandates, strategies, and options to comply with these regulations.

courses.title: College Success Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Assists students in transition to colleges. Provides overviews of college policies, procedures, curricular offerings. Encourages contacts with other students and staff. Assists students toward college success through information regarding effective study habits, career and academic planning, and other college resources available to students. May include English and Math placement testing. Strongly recommended for beginning students. Required for graduation.

courses.title: Orientation To (Specify the Discipline)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the skills which are necessary to achieve their academic goals, to services offered at the college and to the discipline in which they are enrolled. Covers topics such as services at the college including the learning resources center; counseling, and advising; listening, test taking, and study skills; and topical areas which are applicable to their particular discipline or background.

courses.title: Preparation for Employment
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides experience in resume writing, preparation of applications, letters of application, and successfully preparing for and completing the job interview. Assists students in identifying their marketable skills and aptitudes. Develops strategies for successful employment search. Assists students in understanding effective human relations techniques and communication skills in job search.

courses.title: College Survival Skills
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-3 hours. Total 1-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an orientation to the college. Introduces study skills, career and life planning. Offers an opportunity to engage in activities aimed at self-discovery. Emphasizes development of "coping skills" such as listening, interpersonal relations, competence, and improved self-concept. Recommended for students enrolled in developmental courses.

courses.title: Seminar and Project
courses.contact_hours: May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Requires completion of a project or research report related to the student's occupational objectives and a study of approaches to the selection and pursuit of career opportunities in the field.

courses.title: Introduction to Sociology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental concepts and principles of sociology with attention to sociological theory, research methods, and the impact of social inequality. Examines a variety of topics such as culture, race, social class, gender, major social institutions and their role in contemporary society, and the processes of social change. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Cultural Anthropology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Examines the origins, development, research, diversification and evolution of human cultures. Includes exposure to the variability of both Western and Non-Western aspects of culture. Provides an introduction to the nature of culture and its relationship to various social institutions and societies. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Sociology of the Family
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces tools to study family life through the sociological lens. Explores a variety of topics including various familial forms, divorce, and domestic violence.

courses.title: Sociology of Gender
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours, Total 3 hours per week Prerequisite: Ability to read in English at the college level.
courses.description: Analyzes influence of major social institutions and socialization in shaping and changing sex roles in contemporary society. Examines differential access to positions of public power and authority for men and women.

courses.title: Race and Ethnicity
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Considers race and ethnicity as social constructs that deeply affect personal experience and social institutions. Examines the relationships of racial and ethnic groups with each other and with larger society including ideas of racial inequality both individually and systemically. Introduces significant theoretical approaches to the study of race and ethnicity.

courses.title: Social Problems
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the fundamental concepts underlying social problems construction with attention to how these problems are defined, understood and arbitrated. Examines a variety of topics such as researching social problems and policymaking. This is a Passport and UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Spanish I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Beginning Spanish II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 4 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 101 , or two years of successful completion of high school Spanish, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Introduces cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills and emphasizes basic sentence structure. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 102 , or three years of successful completion of high school Spanish, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and introduces complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in target language. Part I of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 201 , or four years of successful completion of high school Spanish, or demonstrated experiential learning, or by placement test, or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop cultural awareness, listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, and emphasizes complex sentence structures. Classes may be conducted in the target language. Part II of II. This is a UCGS transfer course.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop understanding, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Classes conducted in Spanish. May include oral drill and practice. Part I of II.

courses.title: Intermediate Spanish I-II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3-4 hours per week. Prerequisite: SPA 102 or equivalent.
courses.description: Continues to develop understanding, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Classes conducted in Spanish. May include oral drill and practice. Part II of II.

courses.title: Introduction to Women's Studies
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week. Prerequisite: ENG 111 .
courses.description: Introduces interdisciplinary and cross-cultural theories that explore gender, race, and class issues relating to women's lives, past and present.

courses.title: Introduction to Surgical Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Total 2 hours per week. Prerequisite: Readiness for ENG 111
courses.description: Introduces professional practice concepts within the profession of surgical technology with emphasis on the profession and career opportunities. Introduces concepts such as group dynamics, effective communication, organization, prioritization, and delegation. Emphasizes standards of practice and codes of conduct for surgical technologists.

courses.title: DOT Safety Rules and Regulations
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Includes an intensive study of the Department of Transportation and state and local laws and regulations governing the motor carrier industry as applied to the professional operation of commercial vehicles.

courses.title: Preventive Maintenance for Truck Drivers
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the fundamentals of preventive maintenance and inspection procedures for gasoline and diesel powered tractor-trailers. Includes drivelines, brake systems, electrical system and accessories encountered by the professional truck driver.

courses.title: Tractor Trailer Driving
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 12 hours. Total 15 hours per week.
courses.description: Prepares the prospective driver to operate a motor vehicle in a safe and responsible manner. Provides practical training in over-the-road and city driving, including backing skills, and pre-trip inspection. Emphasizes defensive driving.

courses.title: Survey of the Trucking Industry
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an overview of the trucking industry, and the characteristics of the professional truck driver. Emphasizes the uses of technology in the trucking industry, including simulators, mobile information management and communication, and electronic mapping techniques. Provides an introduction to the transportation of hazardous materials and environmental issues.

courses.title: Cooperative Education
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises in on-the-job training for pay in approved business, industrial and service firms, coordinated by the college's cooperative education office. Is applicable to all occupational- technical curricula at the discretion of the college.

courses.title: Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) Remote Pilot Ground School
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Total 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents the aeronautical knowledge required for FAA approved commercial operations as a Remote Pilot with small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) rating. Covers the regulations applicable to small UAS operations, loading and performance, emergency procedures, crew resource management, determining the performance of the small unmanned aircraft, and maintenance/inspection procedures. Prepares students for the FAA written examination required to obtain the Remote Pilot certificate.

courses.title: Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Total 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces students to the history of small Unmanned Aerial Systems (sUAS), surveys current platforms, applications, components, and sensors. Covers the theory of flight, operations, manual flight, maintenance, and required record keeping. Introduces mission planning, crew management, and autonomous control. Emphasizes the ethical, legal, and safe use of sUAS.

courses.title: Introduction to Animal Science
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys the common breeds of small and large domestic animals, including identification, management, and restraint.

courses.title: Introduction to Veterinary Assisting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents basic information about assisting the veterinarian. Includes information about companion animals, primarily dogs and cats.

courses.title: Care and Maintenance of Small Domestic Animals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents basic information about general and veterinary management of small domestic animals, especially dogs and cats. Provides information concerning animal and human safety, animal restraint, nutrition, common diseases, medical terminology, medical history, and other topics related to the care and maintenance of small animals.

courses.title: Veterinary Office Assisting
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents basic information about common business procedures used in veterinary practice. Includes client and staff relationships and veterinary regulations.

courses.title: Introduction to Veterinary Technology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the role of veterinary technicians in veterinary practice. Includes medical terminology, ethics, professionalism, and basic concepts of patient care.

courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology of Domestic Animals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the structure and function of the animal and of all the organ systems of common domestic animals. Includes histology, embryology, and genetics. Includes laboratory dissection and demonstrations.

courses.title: Laboratory Techniques I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces techniques in hematology, urinalysis, and parasitology. Includes other laboratory tests performed in veterinary practice.

courses.title: Animal Breeds and Behavior
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Surveys common species of domestic animals including basic husbandry, care, and handling. Introduces identification of various breeds and their characteristics, including behavior patterns, problems, and solutions.

courses.title: Clinical Practices I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents advanced clinical techniques commonly performed in veterinary practice. Part I of II.

courses.title: Clinical Practices II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Presents advanced clinical techniques commonly performed in veterinary practice. Part II of II.

courses.title: Anesthesia of Domestic Animals
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces the basic principles of anesthesia of common domestic species. Includes techniques of induction, monitoring, and recovery of patients using injectable and inhalation anesthetics.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: On-Site Training
courses.contact_hours: Credit/work ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Specializes in career orientation and training program without pay in selected businesses and industry, supervised and coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Animal Diseases I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Describes animal health and disease, surgical techniques, and animal behavior. Includes demonstrations and selected observation and practice in animal hospitals, clinics, or research laboratories. Part I of II.

courses.title: Animal Diseases II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Describes animal health and disease, surgical techniques, and animal behavior. Includes demonstrations and selected observation and practice in animal hospitals, clinics, or research laboratories. Part II of II.

courses.title: Laboratory Techniques II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 6 hours per week. Prerequisite: VET 115 .
courses.description: Expands concepts introduced in VET 115 including clinical chemistry, cytology, and other laboratory tests performed in veterinary practice.

courses.title: Animal Pharmacology
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies drugs and other medical substances of veterinary importance. Includes their characteristics, usage, measurement, dosage, administration, and also pharmacy management.

courses.title: Introduction to Laboratory, Zoo and Wildlife Medicine
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Focuses on the identification, captive management, restraint and diseases of fish, reptiles, birds, rodents, rabbits, ferrets, primates, wild carnivores, and wild herbivores. Presents the fields of laboratory research zoological medicine.

courses.title: Advanced Clinical Practices III
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week. Prerequisite: VET 121 - VET 122 .
courses.description: Presents advanced clinical techniques commonly performed in veterinary practice.Part I of II.

courses.title: Coordinated Internship
courses.contact_hours: Credit/practice ratio not to exceed 1:5 hours. May be repeated for credit. Variable hours.
courses.description: Supervises on-the-job training in selected business, industrial or service firms coordinated by the college.

courses.title: Introduction to Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1-2 hours. Laboratory 2-3 hours. Total 3-5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces history of welding processes. Covers types of equipment, and assembly of units. Stresses welding procedures such as fusion, non-fusion, and cutting oxyacetylene. Introduces arc welding and plasma arc cutting. Emphasizes procedures in the use of tools and equipment.

courses.title: Shielded Metal Arc Welding (Basic)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches operation of AC and DC power sources, welding polarities, heats and electrodes for use in joining various metal alloys by the arc welding process. Deals with running beads, butt, and fillet welds in all positions. Emphasizes safety procedures.

courses.title: Shielded Metal Arc Welding (Advanced)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Continues instruction on operation of AC and DC power sources, welding polarities, heats and electrodes for use in joining various metal alloys by the arc welding process. Deals with running beads, butt, and fillet welds in all positions. Emphasizes safety procedures.

courses.title: Pipe Welding I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5-6 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches metal arc welding processes including the welding of pressure piping in the horizontal, vertical, and horizontal-fixed positions in accordance with section IX of the ASME code.

courses.title: Pipe Welding II
courses.contact_hours: Laboratory 9 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides practice in the welding of pressure piping in the horizontal, vertical, and fixed positions.

courses.title: Pipefitting and Fabrication
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Reviews basic mathematical skills necessary for the pipefitting trade. Teaches basic methods for fabricating piping offsets, miter-turn fittings, tees, odd angle elbows, 90 degree elbows, and the use of pipefitting and layout tools. May be taken with WEL 126 .

courses.title: Inert Gas Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces practical operations in use of inert gas shielded arc welding. Studies equipment operation, setup, safety and practice of GMAW (MIG) and GTAW (TIG).

courses.title: Welding III (Inert Gas)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies Tungsten and metallic inert gas procedures and practices including principles of operation, shielding gasses, filler rods, process variations and applications, manual and automatic welding, equipment and safety.

courses.title: Pipe and Tube Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hour. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 4 hours per week. Prerequisite: WEL 136 or Instructor Permission.
courses.description: Develops entry level skills for the inert gas tungsten welding process (TIG) with emphasis upon thin and thick wall carbon and stainless piping and tubing.

courses.title: Welder Qualification Tests I
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies techniques and practices of testing welded joints through destructive and non-destructive testing. Part I of II.

courses.title: Welder Qualification Tests II
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Studies techniques and practices of testing welded joints through destructive and non-destructive testing. Part II of II.

courses.title: Welding Drawing and Interpretation
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2-3 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches fundamentals required for successful drafting as applied to the welding industry. Includes blueprint reading, geometric principles of drafting and freehand sketching, basic principles of orthographic projection, preparation of drawings and interpretation of symbols.

courses.title: Gas Metal Arc Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3-6 hours. Total 5-8 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces semi-automatic welding processes with emphasis on practical application. Includes the study of filler wires, fluxes, and gases.

courses.title: Flux Cored Arc Welding (FCAW)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces flux cored semi-automatic welding processes with emphasis on practical application. Includes the study of filler wires, fluxes, and gases.

courses.title: Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW), Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Introduces practical operations in the use of tungsten arc welding and equipment. Studies equipment operation setup, safety, and practice of Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW), Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG).

courses.title: Introduction to Maritime Welding
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours per week.
courses.description: Teaches general welding terms, symbols, and joint designs used by maritime industries. Develops skills to recognize weld defects, develops familiarization of drawings and workmanship specifications used for welding applications in the maritime industry, and certifies the student as a Maritime Industrial Fire Watch.

courses.title: Advanced Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW), Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week. Prerequisite: WEL 164
courses.description: Continues practical operations in the use of tungsten arc welding and equipment. Studies equipment operation setup, safety, and practice of Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW), Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG).

courses.title: Maritime Sheilded Metal Arc Fillet Welding (SMAW I)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours. Laboratory 3 hours. Total 5 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to Maritime Shielded Metal Arc Fillet Welding (SMAW). Focuses on equipment setup, adjustment and maintenance, safety, and electrode selection. Includes preparation of labs to develop welding skills on carbon steels using small and large diameter covered electrodes in all positions on fillet welds. Provides an introduction to specific types of electrodes and base materials used in SMAWI welding.

courses.title: Maritime Shielded Metal Arc Groove Welding (SMAW II)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours, Lab 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to Maritime Shielded Metal Arc Groove Welding and covers equipment setup, adjustment and maintenance, safety, and electrode selection. Includes preparation of labs to develop welding skills on carbon steels using small and large diameter covered electrodes in all positions on groove welds. Provides an introduction to specific types of electrodes in all positions on groove welds. Provides an introduction to specific types of electrodes and base materials used in SMAWII welding.

courses.title: Maritime Flux Core Arc Fillet Welding (FCAW)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours, Lab 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to Maritime Flux Core Arc Welding and covers equipment setup, adjustment and maintenance, safety, and electrode selection, training to develop welding skills on carbon steels using small and large diameter flux-cored electrodes in all positions on fillet and groove welds. Provides an introduction to specific types of electrodes and base materials used in FCAW welding.

courses.title: Maritime Gas Metal Arc Fillet Welding (GMAW)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 2 hours, Lab 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to Maritime Gas Metal Arc Fillet Welding and covers equipment setup, adjustment and maintenance, safety, and electrode selection, training to develop welding skills on carbon steels using small and large diameter bare wire electrodes in all positions on fillet welds.Provides an introduction to specific types of electrodes and base materials used in GMAW welding.

courses.title: Maritime Gas Tungsten Arc Fillet Welding (GTAW)
courses.contact_hours: Lecture 1 hours, Lab 3 hours per week.
courses.description: Provides an introduction to Maritime Gas Tungsten Arc Fillet Welding and covers equipment setup, adjustment and maintenance, safety, and electrode selection, training to develop welding skills on carbon steels using small and large diameter bare wire electrodes in all positions on fillet welds.Provides an introduction to specific types of electrodes and base materials used in GTAW welding.
